title: Pit band at the Gillis Theatre and a proprietor's reading test
summary: Goodwin recalls playing the Gillis, naming the explosion trio of Swanagan, Lovett and Bruce, and being asked if his band could read.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well I think now, I think you'll find more musicians reading music now then you did back in the days when guys like Baby Lovett and myself and some more guys came along because actually I have played theaters -- now I played the Gillis Theater here, which used to exist down on 5th and WALNUT in Kansas City.

The one that burned down and Lovett almost lost his life in this particular theater. There were three musicians there; Harry Swanagan, Baby Lovett and Roland Bruce, who was a great violinist. Harry Swanagan was a great
pianist and the three of them were working in this theater when this explosion came but --
I'm talking about when you were working there?
Well, when I played we had about seven pieces; the guy hired us, you know --
This was a pit band job?

-- for the pit band. You know, we had to play a show. Now this is before I met Baby Lovett. There was a guy there by the name of Larman Mundy, who was a trumpet player and there were seven of us. I can't remember all the names of the other guys right offhand but the proprietor asked us, said, "You fellows read, don't you"? I've got a show to play", and we said, "Yeah". Everybody spoke up, is "Yeah, we can supposed to read. "Bring us the music" Okay, so he did but with the music, when he brought the music he brought us a little story.

He said, "The only reason I'm asking you fellows this is because you have a -- you guys look nice and everything but I have had bands to come in this place that couldn't read a note and believe me, they were some of the greatest musicians I've ever heard and how they played without reading music I don't know".
I said, "Well this is a gift people have, you know", and we played the show there. It went over nice and we stayed
there about three weeks playing the show but these are some things and these are changes in music. Well now, you know, I don't think the same thing prevails now. I mean in music.
